title: Ophthalmic Side Effects of Systemic Medication

chunks.title: Lids, cornea & lens deposits
chunks.tldr: Vortex keratopathy: amiodarone (nearly all, harmless), antimalarials, Fabry. Chlorpromazine: brown deep corneal + anterior lens capsule stellate deposits. Gold: purple glitter (chrysiasis). Silver: grey Descemet (argyrosis). Steroids: PSC cataract.
points: EGFR inhibitors: trichomegaly, blepharitis. Imatinib: periorbital oedema. Ipilimumab: thyroid-eye-like orbitopathy.
Vortex: horizontal line → cat whiskers → whorl below pupil; spares limbus.
Amiodarone vision loss mild (~5%); not a reason to stop; also anterior subcapsular deposits + optic neuropathy.
Antimalarial keratopathy unrelated to dose (unlike retinopathy).
Gold >1500 mg → corneal deposits; harmless.
Amantadine: white punctate opacities + oedema; reversible.
Allopurinol: ↑ cataract risk in elderly.

cards.q: Most common drug cause of vortex keratopathy?

chunks.title: Topiramate effusion & drug uveitis
chunks.tldr: Topiramate (and other sulfonamides, acetazolamide, bupropion): ciliochoroidal effusion → myopic shift + bilateral angle closure within a month. Stop drug, lower IOP (cycloplegia; no PI, no pilocarpine). Uveitis: rifabutin (hypopyon), cidofovir, bisphosphonates (± scleritis), moxifloxacin (BAIT), TNF inhibitors.
points: Topiramate angle closure is not pupil block → PI doesn't help.
Rifabutin uveitis ↑ with clarithromycin, fluconazole (enzyme inhibitors); mimics endophthalmitis.
Cidofovir: fibrinous AAU, low IOP; topical steroid.
Bisphosphonates: within 2 days (sooner IV).
Sulfonamides: SJS.
TNF inhibitors paradoxically cause uveitis/sarcoid.
chunks.hook: Bilateral angle closure + new myopia + migraine pill = topiramate.

cards.a: Ciliochoroidal effusion rotating the lens–iris diaphragm forward (non-pupil block).

chunks.title: Hydroxychloroquine retinopathy
chunks.tldr: Keep dose ≤5 mg/kg real weight/day. Risk 7.5% after 5 yrs; 20–50% after 20 yrs. Earliest sign: parafoveal outer retinal loss on SD-OCT (Asians: more peripheral) → 'flying saucer' → bull's-eye. Screen: baseline, then annually after 5 yrs (OCT + 10-2 fields ± mfERG/FAF).
points: Binds melanin (RPE, choroid); damage can progress after stopping.
Risks: renal impairment, tamoxifen, high dose, long duration, pre-existing maculopathy.
Chloroquine more toxic (risk >300 g cumulative).
Inferotemporal macula affected first.
Ishihara is insensitive.
Stop drug (with rheumatologist) if toxicity suspected.

cards.a: 5 mg/kg actual body weight per day.

cards.q: Earliest sensitive sign of HCQ toxicity?
cards.a: Parafoveal outer retinal (ellipsoid zone) loss on SD-OCT.

chunks.title: Phenothiazines, digoxin & crystals
chunks.tldr: Thioridazine >800 mg/day → salt-and-pepper → RPE/choriocapillaris loss. Digoxin: yellow vision (xanthopsia). Crystalline maculopathy: tamoxifen (inner retinal crystals, foveal cysts), canthaxanthine (tanning pills; doughnut), methoxyflurane (oxalate), nitrofurantoin.
points: Chlorpromazine retinopathy only with huge doses.
Digoxin: also blue/green tints; ERG b-wave delayed.
Non-drug crystals: hyperoxaluria, Bietti, cystinosis, Sjögren–Larsson, gyrate atrophy, MacTel, talc emboli, West African crystalline maculopathy (kola nuts).

cards.q: Drug causing doughnut-shaped glistening macular crystals in tanning pill users?

chunks.title: Other retinotoxic drugs
chunks.tldr: Interferon α: cotton wool spots + haemorrhages (usually reversible). Desferrioxamine: rapid loss, macular greying → mottled pigment, abnormal ERG. Nicotinic acid >1.5 g: CMO without leakage. Poppers (alkyl nitrites): yellow foveal spot, ellipsoid defect.
points: Interferon: also CMO, RVO, disc oedema, muscle palsy.
Niacin maculopathy resolves on stopping.
Poppers: young, bilateral, photopsia; may recover.
chunks.hook: CMO that doesn't leak: niacin, XLRS, taxanes, Goldmann–Favre.

cards.q: Drug causing CMO without fluorescein leakage?

chunks.title: Ethambutol & amiodarone neuropathy
chunks.tldr: Ethambutol: keep ≤15 mg/kg/day (<1% risk; 18% at >35); onset 3–6 months; bilateral central loss, red–green (early blue–yellow) defects, contrast loss → stop (usually recovers). Worse with renal disease, isoniazid. Amiodarone neuropathy: 1–2%, often bilateral, slow, prolonged disc swelling vs NAION.
points: Ethambutol screening: baseline VA + colour; repeat 6-monthly; report any symptoms.
Amiodarone: ~6–9 months after start; ⅓ asymptomatic; 20% end <6/60.
Amiodarone vs NAION clues: no crowded disc, insidious, bilateral, swelling lasting months, other amiodarone toxicity.
Discuss stopping amiodarone with cardiologist.
chunks.hook: Ethambutol: 15 is the limit, 3–6 months is the danger zone.

cards.q: Features favouring amiodarone neuropathy over NAION?
cards.a: Insidious onset, bilateral involvement, prolonged disc swelling, no crowded disc.

chunks.title: Vigabatrin, methotrexate & bevacizumab
chunks.tldr: Vigabatrin: bilateral concentric/binasal field loss, common if cumulative >3 kg; irreversible; baseline + 3-monthly fields/OCT; max 3 g/day. Methotrexate: rare optic neuropathy (folate). Bevacizumab (systemic): rare cortical blindness.
points: Vigabatrin: males higher risk; avoid with other retinotoxic drugs; OCT RNFL thinning may precede field loss.
Methotrexate: check folate, supplement B12/folate.
chunks.hook: Vigabatrin = visual field 'vice' squeezes from the sides.
